problem: VLM-based end-to-end VLN agents inherit semantic priors from pre-training and tend to learn shallow observation-to-action pattern matching, lacking dynamic spatial awareness of how actions change observations over time. Training on samples of widely varying difficulty is also unstable.
motivation: Navigation in 3D needs the agent to understand why observations change (backward, from actions) and how they will change (forward, given an action), which standard VLM pre-training does not teach. Explicit maps or pose regression are heavy or unnatural for VLMs, so the paper seeks lightweight, language-compatible auxiliary supervision that adds no inference cost.
key_idea: Activate dynamic spatial awareness in a VLM by co-training with Action Retrospection (infer the action sequence between two frames) and Future Frame Selection (choose the true next frame among 4 candidates), organized by a tri-factor easy-to-hard curriculum (TriPA).
insight: Both auxiliary tasks help alone and are complementary (R2R-CE SR 46.02 baseline -> 49.37 AR, 47.06 FFS, 51.55 AR+FFS), and TriPA adds a further gain on top (55.06). Training loss is lower and less variable with SpaAct, and the gains grow with instruction length on RxR, suggesting better long-horizon following. Notably, the auxiliary tasks are used only in training, so inference cost is unchanged.
method: Backbone: JanusVLN-style VLM navigator that autoregressively predicts a low-level action from instruction, history frames and current monocular RGB frame.

Action Retrospection (AR): given two frames o_i, o_j from an R2R-CE/RxR-CE trajectory, the VLM generates the executed action sequence with next-token loss; action-balanced to the minority class size; 0.69M samples.

Future Frame Selection (FFS): given history (4 frames), current frame and action, pick the true next frame among 4 candidates (multiple-choice VQA, cross-entropy); negatives are same-trajectory hard negatives plus cross-trajectory ones; action-balanced; 0.69M samples.

TriPA curriculum: difficulty d = 0.6*trajectory (normalized log frame count) + 0.2*instruction (word count) + 0.2*motion (turn density); samples sorted into 4 buckets and sampled by 4 phase-wise weight vectors from easy-heavy to hard-heavy (soft curriculum).
Stage 1 training: L = L_nav + 1*L_ar + 1*L_ffs on 2.4M R2R-CE/RxR-CE nav samples plus the AR and FFS samples.
Stage 2 training: nav loss only, adding 11.7K DAgger trajectories from the Stage-1 model and 155K ScaleVLN trajectories (~10476K samples in total), following JanusVLN.
Inference: only the navigation branch is used with cached history; AR, FFS and TriPA are training-only.

setting.backbone: JanusVLN-based VLM (fine-tuned, following the JanusVLN default architecture)
setting.training_data: R2R-CE + RxR-CE nav samples (2.4M), 0.69M AR + 0.69M FFS samples built from the same trajectories (Stage 1); Stage 2 adds 11.7K DAgger trajectories and 155K ScaleVLN trajectories
setting.observation: monocular RGB (single front camera) plus cached history frames; no depth, odometry or panorama
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: MOVE_FORWARD 0.25 m, TURN_LEFT/RIGHT 15°, STOP
setting.simulator: Habitat (Matterport3D scenes); real Unitree Go2 qualitative deployment

numbers.extra: no external data beyond R2R/RxR-CE training sets (0K)
DAgger + ScaleVLN subset external data (10476K samples)

numbers_note: Ablation (Table 2, R2R-CE val-unseen, stage 1): baseline SR 46.02/SPL 42.24; full 55.06/50.76 (slightly differs in rounding from the 55.1/50.8 in Table 1). Real-world results are qualitative only. The text in the main-results paragraph says 55.0/50.8 for stage 1, inconsistent with the table's 55.1.
results: SpaAct-stage2 reaches SR/SPL 62.2/57.2 on R2R-CE and 58.6/49.1 on RxR-CE val-unseen with only monocular RGB, beating JanusVLN (60.5/56.8; 56.2/47.5) and StreamVLN (56.9/51.9). Stage 1 with no external data beats the 0K JanusVLN (52.8/49.2 -> 55.1/50.8 on R2R-CE).
limitations: Sim-to-real gap: camera setup and embodiment differ between simulation and real robot; real-world evaluation is only qualitative (two examples).
Gains are incremental over JanusVLN in the stage-2 setting (e.g. +1.7 SR on R2R-CE), and curriculum weights/bucket schedules are hand-set heuristics.
Only evaluated on VLN-CE (R2R-CE, RxR-CE) with a single backbone family.
